Prevention: Try to raise nurseries on virgin land.

Apply agricultural lime to raise soil pH to 7.2.
Do not transplant infected seedlings (with swollen roots) as this will spread the disease.

Rotate with non-host crops e.g. cereals (maize) and legumes (groundnuts), long crop rotation of a minimum of seven years, to reduce pathogen population build-up.
Fungicide drenches can be used to prevent the disease in nursery beds (see yellow direct control column).
Monitoring: Check for stunting of plants, uproot and look at the roots.
Look for swollen roots which may also be rotting which may occur due to secondary infections.
Plants may wilt under the slightest water stress.
Wilting might occur when the temperature is high (regardless of moisture) and recover when it is cool.
Wilting leaves may show a red or yellow colouration.
Carry out direct green controls as soon as symptoms are seen.
Direct Control: Uproot and destroy the infected plants by drying and burning.
Metam sodium in a field with clubroot.
Restrictions: Use personal protective equipment when handling and applying pesticides, follow the label recommendations.
Do not eat, drink or smoke when mixing or applying pesticides.
